articles.title: Liquidation isn't triggered by a price — it's triggered by running out of margin
articles.excerpt: Last week roughly $1.6 billion in crypto positions was liquidated in a single day after an exchange reported a theft. Almost none of those traders were wrong about the direction. They were wrong about…
articles.body: Last week roughly $1.6 billion in crypto positions was liquidated in a single day after an exchange reported a theft. Almost none of those traders were wrong about the direction. They were wrong about a rule: how much margin a position must keep to stay open. Here is the mechanism, in the order it actually fires. 1. The price that kills you is not the last traded price Most venues compute liquidation against a mark price — an index built from several spot exchanges — rather than the last trade on their own book. The reason is protective: a single wick on one exchange shouldn't vaporise positions across the market.

articles.body: Most hiring managers decide very quickly whether a CV is worth a second look, and in many cases software screens it before a person does. That means a CV has two audiences: the tracking system and the human reader. The good news is that most rejections come from problems you can fix in one careful rewrite. Disclosure: I am the maker of All Done, a site with 39 free online tools. This post is a cross-post of my guide on All Done, linked at the end. Start with a clear, predictable structure Use a simple order that both people and software can follow: contact details, a short professional summary, core skills, experience in reverse order, then education and certifications. Use standard headings such as Work Experience, Education, and Skills, rather than creative labels.

articles.body: I learned about the useEffect Hook in React and created an e-commerce website. I also learned about component lifecycle and dependency arrays. 1. What is useEffect? useEffect is a React Hook that allows us to synchronize a component with external systems, such as APIs, timers, browser events, and other external resources. It is commonly used to perform side effects in React components. Syntax `import { useEffect } from 'react'; useEffect(() => { // Side effect code }, [dependencies]); ` 2. Why do we use useEffect?
